title: Who Pays for Efficient Inference? Confidence-Based Small-to-Large LLM Routing Across Tasks and Languages
abstract: arXiv:2610.23249v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Small-to-large language model routing can reduce inference cost by escalating difficult inputs while retaining easier ones on a smaller model. Its success, however, depends on identifying examples that benefit from escalation, and the reliability of confidence across multilingual tasks remains unclear. We present a systematic evaluation of confidence-based routing across three model families, four languages, and three task types, covering 72 model, dataset, language, and scale configurations and 42,288 predictions. We compare global confidence routing with random routing, equal-quota confidence routing, and an oracle upper bound. Confidence identifies beneficial escalations on the Belebele reading comprehension and SIB-200 topic classification datasets, with mean correction-detection AUCs of 0.612 and 0.705. At 50% escalation, it improves over random routing by 1.40--4.67 percentage points on Belebele and 2.54--5.63 points on SIB-200. In

translated_title: 谁为高效推理买单？跨任务与语言的基于置信度的小模型到大模型LLM路由
translated_abstract: 小模型到大模型的语言模型路由可以通过将困难输入升级到大模型、同时让较简单的输入留在小模型上处理，从而降低推理成本。然而，其成功取决于能否识别出哪些样本能够从升级中受益，而置信度在多语言任务中的可靠性仍不清楚。我们对基于置信度的路由进行了系统性评估，涵盖三个模型家族、四种语言和三种任务类型，共包括72种模型、数据集、语言与规模的配置，以及42,288条预测。我们将全局置信度路由与随机路由、等额配额置信度路由以及预言机上界进行了比较。结果显示，置信度能够在Belebele阅读理解和SIB-200主题分类数据集上识别出有益的升级，平均纠错检测AUC分别为0.612和0.705。在50%的升级率下，相比随机路由，它在Belebele上提升1.40–4.67个百分点，在SIB-200上提升2.54–5.63个百分点。
tldr: 该论文对基于置信度的小模型到大模型LLM路由进行了迄今最系统的跨语言、跨任务评估（72种配置、42,288条预测），证明置信度信号能够有效识别值得升级到大模型的困难样本，从而在多语言场景下实现质量与推理成本的更好权衡。
en_tdlr: This paper presents a systematic evaluation of confidence-based small-to-large LLM routing across three model families, four languages, and three task types (72 configurations, 42,288 predictions), showing that confidence signals can reliably identify which inputs benefit from escalation to a larger model, outperforming random routing by 1.4–5.6 percentage points at a 50% escalation rate.
